claims.text: An optimized refractory HEA can serve as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Ta, Mo, Nb, and V have intrinsically low neutron-activation cross-sections suitable for a low-activation alloy.
The initial material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic mixture of multiple refractory elements.
Arc melting is a conventional processing route for refractory HEAs.
The initial alloy was developed without compositional fine-tuning for activation properties.
Refractory HEAs possess strong mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
Preferentially selecting low-activation refractory elements can retain both high melting points and robust mechanical performance.
Fusion plasma-facing components must operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K while exposed to plasma species and neutrons.
Carefully balancing the multicomponent alloy composition produces a stabilized refractory-phase microstructure.
Reducing elements that generate long-lived radioisotopes lowers post-irradiation activation.
The high melting points and mechanical robustness of selected refractory elements maintain structural integrity under combined thermal and irradiation loads.
The optimized refractory HEA will have lower long-lived induced activation than conventional tungsten-based plasma-facing materials.
The optimized refractory HEA will have superior high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance compared with conventional tungsten-based plasma-facing materials.
Tungsten is a leading plasma-facing-material candidate because of its high melting temperature, low erosion rate, and low tritium retention.
Tungsten has low fracture toughness and exhibits brittle transgranular and intergranular failure.
Conventional tungsten-based plasma-facing components suffer from significant neutron-induced activation.
Failure to achieve the optimized elemental ratios may produce activation or mechanical performance comparable to or worse than tungsten alloys.
Failure to obtain the intended refractory-phase stability through processing and microstructure control may eliminate the proposed benefits.
